title: Back-pack vacuum filters, muffler and bag care
audience: Cleaners who maintain the filters, bag and internal parts of backpack vacuums used on commercial and residential jobs.
learningOutcomes: Identify the bag, micro-filter, dome filter, sound muffler and cap in a backpack vacuum.
Service each filter and the muffler at the interval the site sets, and reassemble them in the right order.
Recognise when a filter or bag has reached the end of its life and tag it for replacement.

instruction.heading: What filtration does for the machine
instruction.body: A backpack vacuum only performs as well as its airflow allows. A clogged bag, a full cloth filter or a dirty dome filter restricts that airflow, so the machine loses suction and the dust it fails to trap goes back into the room. Regular service of the filters and the muffler keeps the suction at the level the machine was built for. The schedule below is a general guide; the machine maker's manual and the site's rules set the actual intervals.

instruction.heading: The parts and how they sit together
instruction.body: Remove the twist cap on the upper part of the machine first. Under it, a paper micro-filter bag sits inside a micro-cloth filter. The cloth filter can be shaken out and washed, and the paper bag is discarded when full. Lower in the machine is a dome filter that contains a foam medium, and a sound muffler sits at the bottom. The muffler reduces noise and is also a filter in its own right, so it should be rinsed as part of the service.

instruction.heading: Routine service
instruction.body: Empty the micro-cloth filter by shaking it into a bin each time the bag is changed. Hand wash it once a month and let it air dry completely before refitting. Once a week, clean the foam in the dome filter and rinse the sound muffler, then let both dry before refitting. Replace any part that is torn, hardened or no longer holds dust. Before refitting, clear loose dust from the housing with a microfiber cloth, so none of it reaches the new bag.

instruction.heading: Reassembly order
instruction.body: Start with the dome filter and muffler, then slot a fresh paper bag into the cloth filter and seat that pair in place, finishing with the cap. Wipe the exterior of the housing with a dampened microfiber cloth, leave it to dry, and test the machine on a short run before it goes into use. Any machine that loses suction after service should be tagged and checked by the supervisor.

procedure: Put on gloves, and switch the machine off and unplugged before opening it.
Remove the twist cap and set it aside on a clean surface.
Over a bin, withdraw the bag-and-cloth assembly from the housing.
Pull the paper bag out of the cloth filter and discard it.
Shake the cloth filter out. Wash it by hand once a month and let it air dry before reuse.
Clean the foam in the dome filter and rinse the sound muffler once a week, then let both dry.
Sweep loose dust from the housing walls with a microfiber cloth.
Put back the dome filter and muffler first, then insert a fresh paper bag into the cloth filter and screw the cap on.
Wipe the exterior of the machine, let it dry, and run a short test before use.

workedExamples.situation: A backpack vacuum has lost suction in a shared office, and the cleaner finds the cloth filter full of fine dust and the foam in the dome filter grey.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the most likely cause, and what should the cleaner do?
workedExamples.reasoning: A clogged cloth filter and a dirty dome foam restrict airflow, which reduces suction. Clean or replace the filter components following the service steps, refit them in the right order, and test. If suction does not return, tag the machine and report it.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner refits the machine after service but puts the paper bag in before the dome filter is in place.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the problem with this order?
workedExamples.reasoning: The dome filter and the muffler must be in place before the bag is seated. Refitting in the wrong order can leave the bag or the filter out of position, so the machine will not seal correctly and dust can escape.

equipmentAndPpe: Replacement paper micro-filter bags and micro-cloth filters, as stocked.
Bin for dust and used bags.
Mild detergent or water for washing the cloth filter, as the maker permits.
Spare foam for the dome filter, and a replacement muffler where needed.

commonErrors.error: Refitting a wet filter or muffler, which holds dust and can damage the motor.
commonErrors.prevention: Let every filter and the muffler dry completely before refitting.

commonErrors.error: Running the machine with the bag, filter or muffler missing.
commonErrors.prevention: Refit all parts and check the cap is sealed before switching on.

commonErrors.error: Keeping a worn filter in use because it still looks serviceable.
commonErrors.prevention: Replace a filter that is torn, hardened or no longer holds dust, and tag the old part.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Switch off and unplug the machine before opening the housing or removing any part.
Do not operate a machine with damaged or missing filters, a loose cap, or a cracked housing. Tag it and report it.
Do not attempt electrical repairs to the motor or the switch. Those are outside this lesson and should go to the machine's service provider.

qualityStandard: All filters and the muffler are clean and fully dry before refitting.
The bag, filter, muffler and cap are assembled in the correct order and seal properly.
The housing is free of loose dust before the new bag is fitted.
The machine gives full suction on a short test run.
documentationEvidence: Service record for the machine, with the date, the parts cleaned or replaced, and the next service due.
Tag and report for any machine that does not regain suction after service.
summary: A clogged filter restricts airflow and reduces suction.
Clean the cloth filter, dome foam and muffler on the set schedule, and let them dry fully.
Refit the parts in order: muffler, dome filter, bag, then cap.
Tag a machine that does not regain suction, and do not repair the motor yourself.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the most likely cause of a backpack vacuum that has lost suction?
options: A cap that is too tight on the upper part of the machine
A clogged cloth filter or a dirty dome filter restricting airflow
A cord that is too long for the outlet and it rubs on the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: Which order is correct when refitting the backpack vacuum after a service?
options: Cap first, then the paper bag, then the dome filter and muffler and the hose last
Paper bag first, then the cap, with the muffler left out and the dome filter loose
Dome filter and muffler first, then the paper bag in the cloth filter, then the cap

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a cloth filter or dome foam be dried before it is refitted?
options: Completely, because a wet filter or foam holds dust and can damage the motor
Partly, so that it stays damp and traps more dust while the machine is switched on
Not at all, as long as the filter looks clean and the foam feels dry to touch
